answer: Producing a novel, coherent answer each epoch is cheap per alias but prohibitive across thousands, so scale buys less credibility — the attacker cannot simply buy a large, credible flock. This is durable because the trusted grader set only grows through bootstrap capacity, preventing a sudden takeover by a large new flock. In effect, the network makes cheating the most expensive strategy available, which is the closest thing to a Sybil-resistant design that economics allows. Consider a reef as the anchor of the cost.
